title: A prospective randomised study evaluating the impact of post-procedural therapy, individually tailored to the patient’s resistance to antiplatelet agents, on treatment outcomes following interventional therapy for peripheral arterial disease
summary:
The blood vessels in the human body contain, among other things, blood platelets, known as thrombocytes. These thrombocytes play a vital role in blood clotting and in repairing damage to the inner lining of blood vessels. Years of damage to the inner wall of the blood vessels (e.g. due to smoking, high blood pressure or cholesterol deposits) cause the repair processes in the vessel wall to spiral out of control, leading to the formation of calcium deposits that narrow or block the blood vessels. This can lead to life-threatening conditions such as a heart attack, stroke, thrombosis and/or embolism. You are suffering from circulatory disorders in the legs as a result of the narrowing or blockage of the arteries (peripheral arterial disease – PAD). 
A key component of the treatment for this condition is the use of medication known as antiplatelet agents, which prevent blood platelets from sticking together, thereby inhibiting clot formation and excessive repair processes in the vessel walls. Some patients have a natural resistance to these medicines, meaning that the PAs (antiplatelet agents) cannot take full effect, or cannot take effect at all.
The aim of this study is to determine whether a test (Multiplate® test) to assess the effectiveness of antiplatelet agents (aspirin or clopidogrel) and the subsequent individual adjustment of your medication is possible and/or necessary in your case. To this end, we wish to perform the Multiplate® test and determine whether a treatment adjustment is necessary for you or whether we can proceed according to current standards (standard drug therapy). The test must therefore be carried out prior to treatment. This is followed by routine treatment involving balloon and catheter-assisted dilation of the blood vessels or the insertion of a stent. During this medical procedure, small tubes with a wire mesh (stents) are also inserted into the blocked blood vessel or into several blocked blood vessels. This stent is then intended to keep the blood vessel permanently open. This procedure is also routinely performed, for example, to open coronary arteries in the event of a heart attack.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients with symptomatic peripheral arterial disease (PAD), regardless of stage, who are receiving interventional treatment on the lower limbs
- Follow-up of medical history, clinical status and Doppler ultrasound over a 12-month observation period, including medical history assessment, Doppler ultrasound of the legs with ABI measurement, and wound assessment according to the WIFI classification at 3, 6, 9 and 12 months
- Baseline patient compliance
- Guideline-based pharmacological treatment of symptomatic PAD with antiplatelet agents (APAs) and statins
Exclusion criteria:
- Patients receiving anticoagulant therapy
- Intolerance to TAH    
- Dialysis patients
- Patients taking NSAIDs
- Patients with a known reduced response to TAH
- Patients with liver dysfunction
- Patients under the age of 18
- Pregnant women
